thread:
maria: FYI CI size gate tripped on the attention-kernels branch. Fatbin jumped ~22% after adding the async I/O kernels. Build log: `FAILED: size_gate (allowed 45MB)`

devin: ugh, thanks for flagging. Is it the device debug flags or new arch entries? any `nvcc` line in the logs?

maria: Log shows nvcc invoked with our usual flags plus `-g` from the debug profile. But even with `-O3` and `-lineinfo` off we still see the bump. Here's the nvcc line: `nvcc -ccbin g++ -O3 -Xcompiler -fPIC -arch=sm_80 -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 --fatbin -rdc=true -Xptxas=-v -lineinfo -g -o libkernels.fatbin`

samir: -g will add device debug symbols (huge!). CI shouldn't build debug by default for size gate. Which CI job is this? dev-debug or release?

maria: It's the `kernel-build-release` job, but our CMake override picks up `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` from the matrix. Looks like we accidentally included debug for kernels.

liz: suggestion: split out symbol generation from fatbin: build release fatbin without `-g` and then optionally produce a separate debug artifact we store elsewhere. Also strip host-linked symbols.

hao: Agree. We should also audit the `-gencode` list. We currently pass multiple `-gencode` entries including `compute_80,code=compute_80` (ptx fallback) plus sm_80 cubin. Each extra arch creates another cubin/PTX in the fatbin. Trim to only the targets we need for CI.

devin: +1. For CI reproducibility I'd do: `-gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80` (or use the newer `--gpu-architecture=sm_80` pattern), and avoid generating both PTX and cubin unless we need a fallback.

julie: Note: some customers run older drivers => fallback PTX necessary. But for internal CI we can gate size with an explicit list env var: `CI_CUDA_GENCODES=sm_80` and run a separate compatibility build in a different job.

samir: Another lever: use `nvcc --ptxas-options=-v` to inspect register pressure and maybe reduce unrolled kernels or template bloat. But that won't necessarily reduce fatbin size when the kernel codegen is the same.

maria: One weird thing: `-rdc=true` also increases object sizes because of relocatable device code. We added it for device-level linking for the new split kernels. Can we avoid rdc for release build and use link-time consolidation only where necessary?

hao: If we keep `-rdc=true` it's required for device linking (separable compilation). We could mark a couple targets `CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION` ON only when building the debug/dev job. For release, compile monolithically (no rdc) to shrink fatbins.

devin: There's also `cuobjdump`/`nvdisasm` to inspect which sections are largest. I ran `cuobjdump --dump-sass libkernels.fatbin` and the attention kernels were the big chunk. Looks like a lot of duplicated inlined templates across variants.

liz: Action items I propose: 1) change CI matrix so `kernel-build-release` uses `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` and strips `-g`/`-lineinfo`, 2) limit gencode list for size gate via `CI_CUDA_GENCODES`, 3) add a separate `compatibility-fallback` job producing PTX/cubin combos, 4) add a job that runs `cuobjdump` and uploads a size breakdown artifact.

maria: I can send a small PR for (1) and (2). For (4) we can reuse `sizeprofiler` script. Example cuobjdump snippet I used: ```bash
# inspect fatbin sections
cuobjdump --list libkernels.fatbin
cuobjdump --dump-sass libkernels.fatbin | sed -n '1,200p'
```

samir: We should also consider using `--generate-code` vs `-gencode` canonicalization. Newer nvcc supports `-arch=sm_80` which is nicer. Also passing `-Xlinker --strip-all` for the host link step might help. But be careful: stripping host symbols can break stack traces in production. Better to separate strip step for the CI artifact only.

devin: On toolchain drift: CI uses cuda 11.8 on build nodes; the internal dev machines are on 12.x. Different ptx/cubin outputs will affect size. We should pin the CUDA toolchain in the CI job name (e.g., `kernel-build-release-cuda11.8`) and gate the size per-toolchain baseline.

liz: +1. Also add a new CI threshold table keyed by CUDA version + GPU arch set. That avoids false negatives when upgrading toolchains.

maria: Okay I'll open PR with CMake change to prefer `Release` in that job, and a small env var switch for `CI_CUDA_GENCODES`. Will also add a follow-up issue to add cuobjdump artifact collection.

ci-bot: New issue created: #2347 "CI: kernel fatbin size gate tuning and artifact breakdown" (assigned to @maria) :page_facing_up:

julie: Thanks team — if anyone hits the gate locally, run `./build.sh --rel-without-debinfo` and compare `objdump` sizes before pushing. I'm happy to help repro. :+1:

maria: Thanks — PR inbound in ~30m. If it still fails I'll post the CI artifact link here. :eyes:
